source_review.notes: Checked current Linux kernel perf security documentation, Linux man-pages 6.17 perf_event_open semantics, Python 3.14 time and tracemalloc documentation, and the current Valgrind Massif manual. Publisher and bibliographic records were checked for the systems-performance, flame-graph, and performance-analysis references. Platform and permission dependencies are labeled.

evidence: Defined wall, CPU, inclusive/exclusive, allocation, live/peak, RSS, and logical/physical-byte notation.
Checked time, processor-equivalent, byte, MiB, percentage, ratio, sample, and counter scopes.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All ratios name their numerator, denominator, and observation boundary.

evidence: Recomputed phase residuals 2 and 30 ms, detected the 60 CPU/30 wall scope case, and checked 2.8 processor-equivalents.
Recomputed 0.25 read, 1.5 write, and 10%-to-20% compositional profile ratios.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No residual or amplification ratio is treated as a causal label.

evidence: Checked the single-thread CPU-versus-wall premise and its parallel aggregate exception.
Re-derived live allocation conservation and verified that no universal logical/physical I/O inequality exists.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Each identity states the complete-observation and matching-scope premises.

evidence: Reviewed zero and equal time, aggregate CPU above wall, short phases, periodic sampling alias, counter multiplexing, lost events, unresolved stacks, and asynchronous completion.
Reviewed high allocation/low liveness, live-heap/RSS gaps, cache-served reads, amplified writes, profiling overhead, privilege restrictions, and sensitive captures.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unavailable or incomplete evidence remains labeled rather than silently substituted.

evidence: Checked named scope/boundary, correctness, inclusive/exclusive separation, memory-taxonomy separation, I/O-layer separation, counter metadata, and run identity invariants.
Executed four time-scope cases and three fully observed allocation-conservation cases independently.
invariant_checking.notes: Derived outputs retain links to immutable raw profile/run identities.

evidence: Reviewed why one thread cannot accumulate more matching thread CPU than wall time and why sums across workers can.
Reviewed allocation conservation and the cache/amplification counterexamples to a universal cross-layer I/O inequality.
proof_review.notes: Profiler attribution is consistently framed as hypothesis evidence, not automatic causation.

evidence: Audited estimate, sample, count, trace, inclusive, exclusive, residual, hotspot, bottleneck, physical, logical, supported, scaled, and lost language.
Separated tool observation, algorithm model, causal hypothesis, controlled perturbation, and unprofiled end-to-end validation.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No platform counter or memory field is presented as universally portable.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet produced the exact fixture residuals, memory values, and I/O ratios on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
Independent arithmetic covered four time cases, five ratios, and three allocation-conservation fixtures.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The executable reduces captured fixtures; it is explicitly not a live profiler or performance claim.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed benchmark/profile/trace distinctions, time scopes, phases, sampling, stack attribution, counter semantics, memory categories, I/O layers, perturbation, differential profiles, causal validation, and security.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed build and run identity, symbols/unwinding, enabled/running time, event loss, profiler overhead, allocator coverage, mappings, cache state, block/device scope, least privilege, retention, and raw-artifact governance.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter progresses from symptom to discriminating evidence and causal validation, includes one executable reducer, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, profiler-vendor, kernel, hardware-counter, operating-system, storage, privacy, security, or production review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on workload/run identity, tool and event definitions, privilege, clock, scope, symbols, unwinding, sampling, multiplexing, loss, allocation coverage, memory and I/O boundaries, environment, overhead, toolchain, and platform.
